steps.name: Gali
steps.text: What is it this time, Hibiscus? I've humored you and gotten the checkup. You do what you do with the other workers.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's not about the physical screening! You have to be here today, Mr. Gali!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Stop pulling my sleeve, I've got to fill the boss's orders...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Hey! Gimme back my keys!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I finally found an expert who can come in and help find out why everyone in the workshop's conditions have been flaring up with no rhyme or reason!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm not giving you back your keys unless you cooperate!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Hey, stop it, you brat!

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Take it easy, Hibiscus... What's the matter, Gali? Have you eaten yet?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Wallen? Stop her!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: There's no use hiding behind him!

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Yeah, you can't hide now that I've gotten skinnier!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Remember to watch what you eat so you don't regain all that excess body fat!

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: I know, I know.

steps.name: Humorous Worker
steps.text: What happened to the guy who used to complain about the annoying new doctor? Still can't believe Hibiscus managed to win your stubborn ass over.

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: You askin' for a fist to the face? Hibiscus, I caught him drinking beer last night, all those empty cans...

steps.name: Nervous Worker
steps.text: Hey now! Don't listen to him!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Well, I've been monitoring everyone's vitals... Once should be fine, I guess, but don't do it again!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...You sure are patient. The doctors from the last hospital couldn't wait to get away from here once they saw a bunch of Infected.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No wonder the patient records were full of errors. We should continue to work together, Mr. Gali. Rhodes Island treats the Infected with care and attention!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Fine, fine, I'll think about it. Just gimme back my car keys.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Huh? That's a completely different matter! The expert still hasn't...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I know, I know, it's your first mission, you want to look good. Don't worry, I'll put in a good word with your supervisor.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That's not the problem, Mr. Gali! I really do suspect that—
Well, look at that, a personal welcome from the boss?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: What are you doing here in the middle of the day, dressed like that? Do all government employees have this much free time?

spans.text: What are you doing here in the middle of the day, dressed like
? Do all government employees have this much free time?

steps.text: I guess the rumors of you mellowing out have been greatly exaggerated. I'm not here to argue.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Then... Hey, what's that equipment on your back? It's not time for the annual inspection yet! Besides, you're not who handles our inspections—
Forgot to take your meds or something? You think I'd have come on my own without being asked?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Are you Mr. Edgar?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Wait, don't tell me this guy is the expert you were talking about?

spans.text: guy is the expert you were talking about?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Gali! Mr. Gali! I...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: One second.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Yes, I'll take care of the rest... Bye.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The results are in. The safety equipment is really worn-out, with lots of cracks in the isolation shell. No wonder the workers keep getting sick.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Folks from the Engineering Department tell me this part is out of production, and that it'd be cheaper to just buy a new machine.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: A new machine, eh?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I know it's not cheap, but the workers will never get better in this environment.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Alright, we'll get it replaced.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...Really?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: If a few quid is all it takes. We're all old neighbors from the slums.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Thank you! But it might take more than a few quid... here's the catalogue.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...You could buy half my workshop with that kind of cash!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Well, there's also this.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: An industrial equipment subsidy... did you get that from Edgar?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I understand that you might have some history with him, but these are all official documents, and I added comments where the legalese gets confusing.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I can even fill out the form for you, if you're busy. All you'll need to do is review it before signing.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I see... Oh, Hibiscus, your office just called. They want you to go back.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Huh? Why would they call you?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I was so busy I didn't even realize that the contract expired half a month ago. I'll work out your pay...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No need for that, Mr. Gali! I'm here as a volunteer!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: No, but...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's okay, really! I was planning to stay a little longer anyway. I'll talk to the head office.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Cleaning up the workshop, installing the new equipment, plus the necessary safety training... All that will take at least a month. You'll be short-handed.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Once the new equipment is ready, I'll also need to follow-up with everyone, to make sure there's no rebound—

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: It's okay, Hibiscus. You've done enough.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Do you have a lot of stuff? I can take the car out.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...Are you having problems, Mr. Gali?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If money is the issue, I can help you apply for a medication subsidy that all factories that employ Infected are eligible for.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't try to take on everything alone! It's okay to accept help from others once in a while. And I could introduce you to—

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: For heaven's sake, could you just stop?! Has it never occurred to you that you're my biggest problem?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: What do you...?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Do you know how much delay your checkups have caused? My phone's been ringing for two days straight with all the people demanding to know when their orders will be ready!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I... I'm sorry, Mr. Gali, I didn't know the factory was so backlogged. But I've adjusted the treatment plan...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Enough. I know you want to look good, to feel like you've accomplished something on your first mission.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: But first you called Edgar here, and now you want to me stop working and replace my equipment? Everyone could be out on the streets starving by tomorrow!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...Are you that concerned that you won't be able to deliver on time? Don't worry, I've looked it up!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Work delays due to equipment repair and replacement are eligible for city subsidies, legal relief, and health subsidies... for up to a month.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Edgar said that the facility is eligible for an equipment subsidy that will cut the out-of-pocket expense for new machines in half!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Enough! Edgar this, Edgar that! Do you even know who he is? Do you know which noble holds the leash on his collar?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Little factories like us can't afford to miss a deadline. Health subsidies? They'll just end up in somebody else's pocket!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I-I'll get it cleared up, make sure everything is actually in order...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Get back here! Do you still not get it?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Every time you do any of this shit, someone learns about it, and those nobles take another bloody cut out of my pocket!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No wonder there were new inspection stamps on the aging machines... No wonder the supervisor at the city council looked confused when I brought him the files...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Your factory isn't licensed, is it? It's a private sweatshop employed by nobles.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Yes! Do you finally get it? The best thing you can do for me is pack your stuff and get your ass back to that Rhodes Island!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Okay, I'll go, but there's one last thing I want to check first.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Are the results from the previous hospital's checkups accurate, or were they fudged?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Because I don't see how such mild symptoms could deteriorate so much in just a year.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's not a problem with the data, is it? It's the work... you made them trade their lives for money, didn't you?!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: So what if I did? Their lives would be worth even less if I didn't get them these jobs! Where do you think we are, Londinium?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: How many boots do you think I had to lick just to hire the Infected? All so I could take on orders the uninfected workers wouldn't touch with a 10 foot pole!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Are you guys arguing?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No, just talking... About work.

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Whatever. Edgar came back and went around the workshop measuring stuff. And something about taking half a month off?

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Would those big companies even agree to that when we haven't finished their orders? ...Hey, why aren't you guys saying anything? What's going on, Gali?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Just get back to work, Wallen. I'll take care of it.

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: You'll take care of it... Kid, we're sick, not dying. Don't try to take everything on yourself.

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: If the factory's having trouble... you can always take on more orders. We can handle it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Wallen...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Don't worry, I'll let you know if I ever really need help.

steps.name: Wallen
steps.text: Alright, then come and get your grub when you're done here. We saved plenty of meat for you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...They knew?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: They're Infected, not stupid. The only way they can live a better life is to make the most of their already-infected bodies.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But that's only because they don't have a choice. It doesn't mean they have to just sit and take it. It doesn't mean they can't have hope for the future!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Hope? You kidding me?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Do you expect the fat bastards above us to suddenly grow a conscience and start handing out money? Or the workers to eat your bland-ass food every day until they're sick to death of it?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: When you don't have long to live, might as well use that time to earn some cash and make life better now.

spans.text: When you don't have long to live, might as well use that time to earn some cash and make life better

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...Do you really think that's what they want?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Wallen exercises every day, Bard has virtually quit drinking, and Elsa has put away her cigarettes after smoking all her life.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Do you really think they don't care about living longer?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The Infected have the right to be healthy too. They may be willing to give it up for their livelihood, or for their children—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But that's no excuse to expose them to dangerous work, or use them as a trading chip for your profits!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Are you done yet?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Will anything you're saying get me new machines and new jobs that are completely risk-free?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I've done plenty. The stones aren't bloody growing on me. No one forced me to deal with Infected workers, or to put up with your crap.

spans.text: I've done plenty. The stones aren't bloody growing on
. No one forced me to deal with Infected workers, or to put up with your crap.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Now get outta here. I've got work to do.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Gali? You got the files?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...Whatever the nobles behind you are thinking, Edgar, whether they want money or the factory, this is between us. Don't drag a little girl into this.

steps.name: Voice from the Phone
steps.text: Hey! What are you—

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Suppressant dosage and usage guide, protection equipment manual... and a checklist for machine safety devices.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whoa, would you look at that? Hibiscus, of all people, staying up late?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Closure?! Already? How did you...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You thought I'd ignore a late-night request from our little Hibiscus? I've already approved your application for discounted suppressants.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...Thanks.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: As for the private message you sent... Well, it's not like I can't pull some strings to get a sweet discount on this type of equipment...

spans.text: As for the private message you sent... Well, it's not like I
pull some strings to get a sweet discount on this type of equipment...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I just wanted to double-check that you really think this is necessary.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I... I just think that Mr. Gali really does care about his employees.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: So if a discount can change his mind, then maybe all the changes in mindset and improvements in health I've worked so hard for will actually take root.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I know Rhodes Island has no obligation to do whatever I ask, but—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's not what I meant.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: What I meant is we're not talking pocket change, even with a discount. Are you gonna spend years worth of your own salary to buy him the machines if he doesn't agree?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Of course not! My job is just to make one final check on everyone's behalf, and make sure they know what they need to know.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: My powers are limited, but I want to at least do what I can, try to push a little further. That last push may be all that's needed for real change.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Who's sending me work messages at this hour? I'm gonna sue their pants off... Edgar?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Didn't you tell me to send him home because of his feud with the factory owner? What now...?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: They just keep coming! What's wrong with him?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: They aren't for you, Closure. I linked the monitoring bracelet notifications to the terminal.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Why are you still here? Is your ride not here yet?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: There's... something I wanted to confirm with you. Were you checking on the machines in the workshop last night?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: You were monitoring me?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You left in a hurry after yesterday's checkup and didn't take off your bracelet. I got a notification on my terminal about abnormal Originium activity.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Ah, forgot about that. Here.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Now get going if you're done. I was just making sure Edgar didn't mess with anything... What's the matter?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I... I ran an imaging scan last night, which showed a Blood Originium-Crystal Density of 0.2u/L... the same as when I was diagnosed with Oripathy.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...What do you mean?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Have you ever considered the possibility that you've been... infected?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Are you kidding me? There must be something wrong with your equipment. I never go in the workshop without my protective suit. You have any idea how much that cost me?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You bought your suit from the hospital you worked with before, didn't you?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Yeah, what about it?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Why would you trust a doctor who can't even screen properly out of fear of the Infected to take their preventative measures seriously?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...You're talking crap! I always see the best doctors for my checkups!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: And if I'm really Infected, why don't I feel anything? Show me the report! Damn it... what's with all these figures and diagrams?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's the estimated growth trend of your Blood Originium-Crystal Density. Mr. Wallen told me that the high-risk work began last March. Working off your current data...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: No! This can't be happening to me!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Look at all this medicine! It wasn't cheap getting it delivered from Columbia! I've been taking it for so long, I should've developed resistance to it!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...Say something! The report's fake, right? So that I'll buy your products?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Gali, please, calm down...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: And just tell me while you're at it...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: What's with that look on your face? You're laughing at me, aren't you? Stop looking at me like that!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I said, stop looking at me like that! You're happy that I'm Infected, aren't you? You think it's karma that I'm joining your little Infected family?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...I'd never wish that on anyone, no matter how much I dislike them. The uninfected can never understand the pain faced by the Infected.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I don't need your preaching! I'm not gonna become trash like you people, even if I'm Infected!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: My factory... I have enough money to pay for treatment for the rest of my life! I... I...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I haven't even left this bloody place yet... There's still so much I had to do...

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Dammit all, I don't want to die...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: No one does. But it takes a lot of effort just to live. And courage, to keep one's desires in check. And to do all you can to live a better life, no matter how dire the situation.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: There is nothing funny about what you believe are futile efforts.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Once the rocks show up, I won't be able to negotiate with those people anymore... I'll have to find someone else to take over the factory. The fires have to stay lit.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: It's not a matter of a few days... How long can I keep living like a normal person, if I do things your way?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: ...For a long time. Congratulations.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Congratulations?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're very fortunate. While your crystal density has passed the pathological threshold, you haven't developed any symptoms.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Which means you're not technically Infected yet. Your condition will improve as long as you stay away from sources of infection, wear proper protection, and receive appropriate treatment.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...This isn't a joke, right?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's not. You're one step away from full-blown Oripathy, and you should be wary of the organizations that you used to work with.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: As for why I didn't tell you this right off the bat... I wanted you to know how the Infected feel.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...I don't need you to tell me! I know their situation better than you do!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I thought you might have forgotten.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: The people here see you as a kid from the slums who made it big and gave back to his old neighborhood.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Even as their health and circumstances deteriorate, all they ever talk about is how hard things are for you, and how they can help you cut costs.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: They can hardly make ends meet themselves...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I don't believe that someone they all trust and care for so much is only doing this to exploit them.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: 'It's okay if the equipment is a little old; it's okay to take a few more orders...'

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Those kinds of thoughts are like the crystals in your bloodstream, rising to the surface whenever they accumulate. And they must be prevented, just like Oripathy.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Here are the subsidy application forms from Rhodes Island, including suppressants and the equipment that needs to be replaced. The channels are plenty discreet.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Our relationship is just client and contractor. Whatever decision you make from here on is none of my business.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But at least try not to let those people down.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Alright, my ride is here. Goodbye, Mr. Gali.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Wait, the forms you brought... Let's talk about them. And I want to speak to your supervisor too—

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Stop rushing me, dammit! You in a rush to go to hell or something?
Gali! I've got your stuff here! Now come out of your room!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Put it over here, it'll make it easy to move that machine. Hey, this cord isn't the original, is it?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I should ask the office to send a proper engineer... Hey, wear your gloves properly!

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...So which bigshot ordered you to bring in all these new machines?

steps.name: Edgar
steps.text: Did it ever occur to you that maybe I was moved by her sincere pleas and found a conscience?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: I might've believed it five years ago.

steps.name: Edgar
steps.text: Yes, and I know you still hold a grudge ever since I withdrew my investment and took a job for a noble on the city council, but I needed money for my dad's treatment.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Spare me, that's none of my business.

steps.name: Edgar
steps.text: Well, whatever you say... It was the higher-ups who forced these orders for military parts on you, wasn't it?

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: ...How did you know?

steps.name: Edgar
steps.text: Someone would've swallowed up this little factory of yours a long time ago if I didn't.

steps.name: Edgar
steps.text: You should take on some normal orders now that you've got the new machines. I've already talked to the guy at the city council who handles factory licenses.

steps.name: Gali
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Mr. Wallen? I said we didn't need your help! The equipment testing is bad for your health! Shoo!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Me? I'm alright, I'm wearing protective gear, and I can use Arts... Fine, I'll go with you!
The number you are calling is currently unavailable. Please leave a message after the tone.
Hibiscus! I've called you three times already! How long is this gonna take, seriously? The guys from A1 are gonna break down my door if you don't get back to me!
Anyway, I wanted to say it's really impressive how you got the situation under control in such a short time. And on your first field mission, too. You even got Edgar to buy the new machines.
Patience, professionalism, sticking to your guns, predicting the client's needs... We should work together on a business venture some time.
Seriously though, come back soon! We're holding a party to celebrate your success and we need the guest of honor!
